chapter: Clubs, publishers, unions and life in Denver
title: Fletcher's Weber piano and the 139th Street house
summary: Horace keeps Fletcher's Weber grand with his fingernail scratches; it came from the New York home at 228 West 139th Street, where Fletcher's wife Leora, a trumpet and sax player and excellent copyist, lived. They had no children.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: Uh-huh. This piano here, you -- I think the first day I was here you said that this had been Fletcher's piano. Is that correct?
This is Fletcher's piano here. In fact, from where we're sitting, if you'll notice right up over the black keys where my wife is pointing --
Yeah, lot of scratches.
Some scratches?
Yeah.
Those are Fletcher's fingernail prints. He had long fingers, and sometimes they would go up against there.
Just get right at --
He would scratch some of the brown off, you know. I've never touched that, and I never will.
No, don't.
I wanted to leave that from here? (Unintelligible). Can you see them (unintelligible)? It's a Weber.
Oh, yes, especially in the lower register, below middle C. Yeah, it's a Weber Aeolian.
Man, Those are his fingerprints; he scratched on those things, but To me it's a classic.
Yeah, that's great. That's a baby grand there, probably about a five foot or four and -- four foot eight inches or something.
And the top of it is heavy. I mean my wife wants it moved around or moved somewhere, you know, with the rugs and all, and I'm telling you, just one section of it; you lift up, you were panting.
Do you know where Fletcher acquired that or where did he keep that? Was this like in New York or Chicago or --
This was in his New York home. And if you'll notice, it's got all inlaid material there.
Right, below -- down below the keys.
It's an excellent piano, and it's in excellent shape. And it stays pretty well in tune. We're
talking about something in New York, 228 West 139th Street.
That's where he lived?

Yes. He lived there for many years. Of course, his wife, Leora, used to keep all of her instruments there. You know she played the trumpet, the saxophone too. She was an excellent copyist. She did most of Fletcher's copying, and her writing, her copying was easy for the musicians to read. It was just beautiful. You've seen some of that work.
Uh-huh, right. This is just totally out of my own ignorance. Is she living?
No. She passed quite a few years ago.
And again this is my ignorance. Did Fletcher have children?
No, Fletcher didn't have any.
